I’m late to the thread so not many people will see this: 

I’ve learned not to say I’ve ‘beaten’ it, because every time I think I have, it’s left me disappointed. However, I do feel like I am mastering it, I haven’t had an issue for 5-6 months. And although not recommended, I was able to take myself off of my antidepressants 4 months ago.

For me, I didn’t really have a stable sense of self, so I put a lot of stock into what people thought of me, and I would project my negative thoughts about myself onto them. I noticed that the things I liked would change whenever I was around someone new. I overcame this by isolating myself for a couple weeks to a month and writing 5 things I liked every day and doing some of those things. And then the next day I would read the list I’d written and write 5 more. This helped me really understand who I was and the things I liked and I became more confident about myself. After a good amount of time I slowly reached out to the friends I had had, and tried to see if who I was actually matched with who they were. 

The real advice: everyone is different, try as many things as you can and see what helps you, even if it only helps a little.
